newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 9.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary were invited to join NATO yesterday. Czech politicians see the invitation as an entry ticket to acknowledged democracy. Many said NATO membership means not only guaranteed security for the Czech Republic, but also a share in world defence.

- Floods worsened throughout most of the east yesterday and moved to some areas in southern Moravia. Not only small villages, but also cities like Prerov and Sumperk were isolated. The rain should stop today. Although the numbers are not confirmed, eight people have died and 10 are missing.

- In the coming days, the chairman of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), Michael Zantovsky, and the chairman of Polish Solidarity, Marian Krzaklewski, want to establish a joint Atlantic committee, to deal with cooperation between the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary on their way into NATO.
- Health insurance companies and emergency doctors reached an agreement over point value for medical work -- 77 hellers per point with limited work hours.

- Environmental activists, which organised the blockade at the construction site of the Temelin nuclear power plant, decided to end their blockade today at noon, after which they will go to help in flooded areas.
- Yesterday, parliament approved the cabinets proposal to increase value added tax on fuel and energy from five to 22 percent, but a proposal for consumer taxes was not approved.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Inflation in June over May was 1.2 percent. At 7.9 percent, the avergae rate for the last 12 months is for the first time below eight percent.
- Although insurance companies cannot estimate total losses caused by the floods, it is clear that the extent of damage is the largest in the history of the Czech Republic.
- Cabinet should discuss a transport strategy, an analysis on internal trade and store franchises and a proposal for a law on public orders at its regular Wendesday meeting.

- Parliament yesterday called on the cabinet to present a proposal for a law on the travel industry by the end of September this year, which would protect clients' interests when travel agencies go bankrupt.
- For the first six months of this year, Plzensky Prazdroj sold nearly 2.2 million hectolitres of beer, a year-on-year increase of 20 percent.

PRAVO - Finance Minister Ivan Pilip on Tuesday proposed parliament to allow 900 million crowns from government reserves to go to fix damages caused by the floods, which parliament approved. The cabinet wants to use another 100 million crowns from its own reserves.
- Corporate income taxes will decrease next year to 35 percent from 39 percent, according to a parliament decision.
- Bank IPB wants to sell its majority stake in dairy Jihoceske Mlekarny. According to the dairy's general director, Milan Teply, the management is interested in buying the stake.
- From Wednesday, Komercni Banka will decrease its reference rate by 1.2 percentage points to 16.4 percent and its base rate by 1.05 percentage points to 14.65 percent.
- On Tuesday, parliament approved the closing state balance for 1996 and agreed to cover last year's deficit of 1.5 billion crowns by issuing government bonds.
LIDOVE NOVINY - President Vaclav Havel will announce at a press conference on Saturday if he will run again for president.
- Parliament did not approve any declaration over the cabinet's report on its activities this year, which was requested by the opposition.

- Due to floods in Moravia, Skoda Mlada Boleslav stopped production of Felicia automobiles because it has not received necessary parts from some Moravian companies that have been forced to close down.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
